case_name: Minerva Talkies, Bangalore and Others v State Of Karnataka & Ors. Etc.
facts: The appellants/petitioners hold licences for exhibiting cinematograph films in their cinema theatres under the Act and the Rules in Form prescribed by the Rules.
The Rules and conditions contained in the Licence (Form F) do not prescribe any restriction on the number of shows of films which a licensee can exhibit in his theatre.
Condition No. 11 of the licence provides that: 'No cinematograph exhibition shall continue after such time not later than 1.00 a.m.'

Normally, the cinema owners were holding four shows but later on, they increased it to five shows in a day starting from 10 a.m. to 12 noon, 12 noon to 3 p.m., 3 p.m. to 6 p.m., 6 p.m. to 9 p.m., and 9 p.m. to 12 a.m.
Thus the cinematograph films were being exhibited continuously from 10 a.m. to mid-night, which caused a number of problems.
issues: Whether Rule 41-A of the Karnataka Cinemas (Regulations) Rules has been made 'for purposes of the Act',
Whether Rule 41-A places unreasonable restrictions on the appellants' right to carry on their business of exhibiting cinematograph films in violation of Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.
petitioner_arguments: The provisions of the Act do not confer any power on the State Government to regulate the number of shows,
The restrictions imposed by the impugned Rule 41-A limiting the number of shows to four did not fall within the purview of S. 19 of the Act.
The restriction placed by Rule 41-A was unreasonable and violative of appellants' fundamental right to carry on their business under Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.
respondent_arguments: The purpose of the Act is to regulate exhibition of cinematograph films in licensed premises,
The power of regulation of exhibition of cinematograph films was wide enough embracing the power to limit the number of shows.
The restriction placed by the impugned Rule was reasonable and made in the public interest.
court_reasoning: The declared will of the legislature and the policy and purpose of the Act are discernable from the title, preamble and the express provisions of the Act.
The legislative will is declared by the Preamble of the Act which seeks to deal with the subject of enactment.
The main purpose of the Act is to regulate the exhibition of cinematograph films in places in respect of which a licence for that purpose may be issued.
holding: All the writ petitions were dismissed.
The impugned Rule 41-A was held to be validly framed to carry out the purposes of the Act.
